name: DataLoader
purpose: Batch and dedupe per-request loads from N-per-resolver patterns into one bulk fetch per key-type per tick.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from typing import Hashable, Protocol, TypeVar, runtime_checkable

K = TypeVar('K', bound=Hashable)
V = TypeVar('V')

@runtime_checkable
class DataLoader(Protocol[K, V]):
    async def load(self, key: K) -> V: ...
    async def load_many(self, keys: list[K]) -> list[V]: ...
    def prime(self, key: K, value: V) -> None: ...
    def clear(self, key: K) -> None: ...

invariants.rule: Within one tick, identical keys resolve to the SAME result instance (identity-preserving cache).
Batch fn receives keys in caller-insertion order; returned values correspond positionally.
If batch fn raises, ALL waiting loaders for that tick receive that exception.
clear(k) removes cache entry and does NOT cancel an in-flight batch containing k.
Max-batch-size cap honored; overflow splits into the next batch.

extension_contract: Adopters pass a batch_fn(keys) -> Awaitable[list[values]] and an optional max_batch_size. Subclasses MAY override _schedule_dispatch for non-event-loop schedulers but MUST preserve invariants 01-05. The cache map itself is sealed; policy changes use prime() / clear().
consumption_example:
loader = InMemoryDataLoader(batch_users, max_batch_size=500)
u1, u2 = await asyncio.gather(loader.load(42), loader.load(7))
why_essential: Without DataLoader every GraphQL resolver or nested serializer reinvents N+1 avoidance manually; the ad-hoc variants diverge on cache key, batching, and error propagation and leak across requests.
alternatives_considered: Manual bulk-fetch at the top of each resolver — unmaintainable beyond 5+ resolvers sharing a key.
Request-level memoization decorator — dedupes but does not batch; leaves N+1 fan-out untouched.
Global cache (Redis/LRU) — different problem; does not batch and risks per-tenant leakage.
